title: ci: add pull request unit test gate
body:
As I like the project a lot and have some ideas in mind, I think it makes sense to introduce a lightweight pull request gate, which at least runs the unit tests for the project.

## Summary

- run the Vitest unit suite for pull requests and pushes to `main`
- add regression coverage for imported drum settings and strengthen upload/library tests
- scope coverage reporting to application source and document the testing roadmap
- fix state mutation in library sorting and the imported drum preset state key uncovered by tests
- 
## Notes

- End-to-end tests are intentionally not part of this gate.
- Repository branch rules must require the `Unit tests / test` check to block merges.
- `npm run lint` is not included because the current repository baseline has 345 errors and 24 warnings.

title: Feature: Drum tool take longer sample and split using auto-detect transients
body:
# User Story: Automatic Transient Detection

**As a** musician using OP-PatchStudio  
**I want to** upload a longer drum loop and have it automatically split into individual hits  
**So that** I can quickly create drum presets without manually cutting samples

## Acceptance Criteria

**Given** I upload a longer audio file with multiple drum hits  
**When** I choose "detect transients"  
**Then** the system should:
- Analyze the audio and detect individual drum hits
- Show a preview with detected markers on a waveform
- Allow me to adjust sensitivity and hit duration
- Split the file into individual samples when confirmed
- Assign each hit to an available drum slot

**Given** the samples are created  
**When** I review the results  
**Then** I should be able to:
- Edit individual sample settings
- Reorder or delete unwanted samples
- Use the samples immediately in my drum preset

This would save musicians significant time when converting drum loops into individual samples for OP-XY drum presets.

title: Feature: Companion App: System/App Audio Recording and Integration with Webapp
body:
## Overview

Expand the PatchStudio companion app to support recording system and inter-application audio on Windows, macOS, and Linux. This feature will enable users to record audio from other desktop programs (such as DAWs or virtual instruments) – not just microphones or audio interfaces – and send the recorded audio directly to the PatchStudio webapp for use as samples or tape tracks.

## User Story

As a user, I want to record the audio output from any software on my computer (e.g., Arturia V Collection, a DAW, or YouTube) and send it directly to PatchStudio, so I can easily sample and edit sounds from any source, not just from microphones or audio interfaces.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Provide a UI in the companion app for selecting the system/output device or a specific audio device (including virtual and loopback devices).
- Allow recording of system or application output audio on:
  - **Windows:** via WASAPI Loopback (using NAudio or CSCore).
  - **Linux:** via PulseAudio/PipeWire (using libpulse/simple or invoking parec/CLI tools).
  - **macOS:** via CoreAudio, with user guidance to install BlackHole or another virtual audio driver for system audio capture.
- Guide the user through setup, especially for macOS (offer setup instructions and checks for BlackHole or similar).
- Allow recorded audio to be streamed or sent as a file to the PatchStudio webapp via local HTTP/WebSocket or another IPC mechanism.
- Provide status/feedback in the app for successful recording, transfer, and possible errors.
- Integrate this functionality alongside MTP file transfers in the companion app, sharing device and session management where possible.
- Abstract the platform-specific audio capture logic behind a common interface (e.g., `IAudioRecorder`), and document any platform-specific limitations or extra install requirements.
- Offer user-selectable options for audio format, sample rate, and channel count where possible.

## Implementation Notes
- Use .NET 6/7+ and Avalonia UI for cross-platform desktop app development.
- For Windows, use NAudio's WASAPI loopback capture.
- For Linux, use PulseAudio with .NET bindings or invoke parec, capturing output as a stream or file.
- For macOS, use a CoreAudio .NET wrapper (such as CoreAudio.NET) and require/install BlackHole (open source) or equivalent; provide clear, automated guidance in the UI.
- Create a service interface (e.g., `IAudioRecorder`) and implement per-platform classes: `WindowsAudioRecorder`, `LinuxAudioRecorder`, `MacAudioRecorder`.
- Use Avalonia UI to present device selection, progress/feedback, and error reporting.
- Integrate with the PatchStudio webapp via a local HTTP/WebSocket server; allow the webapp to request a recording or upload a file automatically when finished.
- Ensure robust error handling, user feedback, and documentation for setup and troubleshooting.

---

This issue tracks the implementation of cross-platform audio capture (including system/app audio) and PatchStudio webapp integration in the companion app, alongside MTP transfer features.

title: Feature: OP-1 and OP-1 field Tape Studio: Add, edit, split, and export samples for tape tracks
body:
## Overview

Implement a Tape Studio feature for Teenage Engineering OP-1 and OP-1 field devices, allowing users to add, split, move, edit, and export samples/data to the individual tracks within an OP-1 tape file (AIFF format).

## User Story

As an OP-1 or OP-1 field user, I want to add, split, move, and edit samples on my tape tracks, and export the resulting tape back to my device, so I can create and edit music in a DAW-like environment tailored to OP-1 tape workflows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Support loading OP-1 and OP-1 field tape (AIFF) files and parsing tracks.
- Allow users to add samples or audio data to any track and position.
- Provide editing tools: split track, move regions, trim, delete, crossfade, and basic audio edits.
- Allow exporting edited tape files back to OP-1/OP-1 field-compatible formats.
- Visual track editor UI with waveform display, drag-and-drop, and snapping to bars/beats.
- Support undo/redo for tape editing actions.
- Handle device-specific tape format differences.

## Notes
- Research OP-1 and OP-1 field tape file structure for editing compatibility.
- Consider batch import/export and integration with PatchStudio sample library features.
- Ensure all exports are compatible with OP-1/OP-1 field tape requirements.

---

This story tracks the development of Tape Studio editing tools for OP-1 and OP-1 field tape workflows in PatchStudio.

title: Feature: Implement OP-1 and OP-1 field tape backup and storage support
body:
## Overview

Add features to PatchStudio that allow users to back up, restore, and manage tape data from Teenage Engineering OP-1 and OP-1 field devices.

## User Story

As an OP-1 or OP-1 field user, I want to easily back up and restore my tapes, as well as manage (rename, archive, organize) tape storage, so I can protect and organize my musical ideas.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Provide tape backup functionality for both OP-1 and OP-1 field, supporting their specific file formats and structures.
- Allow restoring previously backed-up tape data to the device.
- Enable management of tape backups, including renaming, archiving, and organizing tapes within PatchStudio.
- Offer clear UI flows for backup/restore, with device detection and error handling.
- Document the backup/restore process and any device-specific limitations.

## Notes
- Research differences in tape data format between OP-1 and OP-1 field.
- Consider incremental backup options or version history for tapes.
- Ensure that data integrity checks are performed on backup and restore.

---

This story tracks the implementation of OP-1 and OP-1 field tape backup, restore, and storage management in PatchStudio.

title: Feature: Integrate Freesound.org and other online free sample libraries for drum and multisample samples
body:
## Overview

Add support for searching, browsing, and importing samples from Freesound.org and other online free sample libraries directly into PatchStudio for use in drum and multisample instruments.

## User Story

As a user, I want to search and import drum and multisample sounds from online free sample libraries (such as Freesound.org) so I can quickly expand my sample collection without leaving PatchStudio.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Integrate Freesound.org API for searching and importing samples (with proper attribution/license display).
- Research and support additional reputable free sample libraries (provide a way to add more in the future).
- Allow previewing samples before import.
- Support importing samples directly into drum kits or multisample instruments workflows.
- Display license and attribution requirements for imported samples within the app.
- Provide options to filter search results by type, license, duration, etc.

## Notes
- Consider OAuth or API key flows for Freesound.org if required by their API.
- Explore plugin-based architecture to allow community-contributed sample library integrations.
- Ensure compliance with all licensing requirements from each provider.

---

This story tracks the implementation of online free sample library integrations for drum and multisample instruments in PatchStudio.

title: Feature: Add support for creating OP-1, OP-1 field, and OP-Z drum presets
body:
## Overview

Implement functionality that enables users to create drum presets compatible with the Teenage Engineering OP-1, OP-1 field, and OP-Z devices within PatchStudio.

## User Story

As a user, I want to easily create and export drum presets for my OP-1, OP-1 field, and OP-Z, so I can use custom drum kits on my hardware synthesizers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Provide preset creation workflows tailored to OP-1, OP-1 field, and OP-Z requirements (sample format, folder structure, naming conventions, etc.).
- Allow importing and arranging individual drum samples.
- Export drum kits in formats directly compatible with each device.
- Include device-specific options (e.g., OP-1 field's higher sample rate support).
- Validate preset and sample compatibility before export.
- Offer documentation or tooltips explaining the export process for each device.

## Notes
- Research format differences and compatibility quirks between OP-1, OP-1 field, and OP-Z drum presets.
- Consider templates or wizards to streamline the preset creation process for each device.
- Explore open-source libraries or resources for working with these formats if available.

---

This story tracks the implementation of drum preset creation for OP-1, OP-1 field, and OP-Z devices in PatchStudio.

title: Feature: Add internet radio recording feature for sampling
body:
## Overview

Implement a feature that allows users to record samples directly from internet radio streams within PatchStudio, expanding the range of creative sampling sources.

## User Story

As a user, I want to listen to and record segments from internet radio stations, so I can easily capture unique sounds and music to use as samples in my projects.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Integrate an internet radio player that supports popular streaming formats (e.g., MP3, AAC, OGG).
- Allow browsing or entering URLs for various internet radio stations.
- Provide real-time recording functionality while a stream is playing.
- Automatically save recorded samples in the user's library for further editing or use.
- Display metadata (station name, track info if available) with each recording.
- Implement UI controls for play, pause, record, and stop, as well as a visual indicator for recording status.
- Ensure compliance with copyright and legal considerations—display a warning or disclaimer before recording.

## Notes
- Research open APIs or directories for radio station listings (e.g., Radio Browser, SHOUTcast).
- Consider features for trimming, tagging, and organizing recorded samples after capture.
- Explore possible limitations or restrictions based on platform (browser, OS).

---

This story tracks the implementation of internet radio recording for sampling in PatchStudio.

title: Feature: Add dark mode support to PatchStudio
body:
## Overview

Implement a dark mode theme for PatchStudio, providing users with an alternative visual appearance that is easier on the eyes in low-light environments.

## User Story

As a user, I want to switch PatchStudio to a dark mode theme, so I can reduce eye strain when working at night or in dark rooms, and personalize my user experience.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Add a toggle or automatic detection for dark mode (based on system/browser preference).
- Apply a consistent dark color palette to all UI components, overlays, and dialogs.
- Ensure all text, icons, and controls remain readable and accessible in dark mode.
- Maintain high contrast ratios and accessibility standards throughout the interface.
- Persist user preference for dark mode between sessions.
- Allow easy switching between dark and light modes from the settings menu or top-level UI.

## Notes
- Consider using CSS variables or a theming framework for easier maintenance.
- Test thoroughly for color contrast, especially on key workflow screens.
- Plan for future expansion to more themes or custom color schemes.

---

This story tracks the implementation of dark mode support for PatchStudio.

title: Feature: Add lazy chop feature to Drum Tool
body:
## Overview

Implement a "lazy chop" feature in the Drum Tool, allowing users to quickly slice samples into multiple regions based on manual pad-triggered playback during live sampling or sample import.

## User Story

As a user, I want to perform lazy chops in the Drum Tool by triggering pads in rhythm while a sample plays, so I can easily create custom drum kits or chopped loops without detailed waveform editing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Enable a mode in Drum Tool where user-triggered pads mark slice points during sample playback.
- Allow live sample playback with real-time chop marker placement.
- After playback, automatically split the sample at the marked points and assign each region to a drum pad.
- Provide an option to quantize, adjust, or fine-tune slice points after recording.
- Support undo/redo and clear all slices functions in lazy chop mode.
- Display visual feedback for playback position, slice markers, and assigned pads.
- Ensure workflow is intuitive for both live sampling and sample import scenarios.

## Notes
- Reference "lazy chop" workflows from popular hardware samplers (e.g., Akai MPC, Roland SP series).
- Integrate with existing sample editing and pad assignment infrastructure in Drum Tool.
- Consider future expansion for auto-slice, transient detection, or grid-based chopping modes.

---

This story tracks the implementation of the lazy chop feature for the Drum Tool in PatchStudio.

title: Feature: Add cloud backup and preset sync for OP-XY
body:
## Overview

Implement cloud backup and preset synchronization features for OP-XY devices within PatchStudio, using the companion app as the bridge between local device storage and cloud providers.

## User Story

As a user, I want to automatically or manually back up my OP-XY projects, samples, and presets to a cloud provider (e.g., Google Drive, Dropbox), and sync presets between devices, so my work is always safe and accessible.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Integrate cloud storage providers (Google Drive, Dropbox, etc.) via OAuth or secure authentication.
- Allow users to configure accounts and choose backup/sync destinations from the web interface.
- Enable full and incremental backups of OP-XY content via the companion app.
- Support restoring backups from the cloud to any connected OP-XY device.
- Allow users to sync selected presets/projects across multiple devices via the cloud.
- Provide clear progress, status, and error feedback during backup and sync operations.
- Ensure data security and privacy (encryption in transit, secure token storage, etc.).

## Notes
- Consider using existing cloud SDKs/libraries in the companion app for simpler integration.
- Make sync/backup operations user-friendly and non-intrusive.
- Architect for future expansion to other cloud services.

---

This story tracks the implementation of cloud backup and preset sync features for OP-XY devices in PatchStudio.

title: Feature: Implement OP-XY backup and file browser via companion app
body:
## Overview

Add support for seamless file browsing and backup/restore functionality for the OP-XY device using a native companion app.

## User Story

As a user, I want to connect my OP-XY to PatchStudio via a companion app, so I can browse, backup, and restore all projects, samples, and presets from a web-based interface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Develop a cross-platform companion app (Windows, macOS, Linux) that:
  - Connects to the OP-XY device via MTP
  - Exposes a local API for communication with the PatchStudio web app (e.g., REST or WebSockets)
- Allow the web app to:
  - Detect when the companion app is running
  - Browse files and folders on the OP-XY in an Explorer-like UI
  - Upload/download/delete/rename/move files and folders via the companion
  - Trigger full or partial device backups (projects, samples, presets) to the user's computer
  - Trigger restores from backup archives to the OP-XY
- Use a custom protocol (e.g., op1fun://) or local server (localhost) for launching/connecting the companion app
- Provide clear user feedback for connection status, operations in progress, and errors

## Notes
- Reference OP1.fun's approach (custom protocol + companion app)
- Consider security implications of local APIs and user device access
- Design APIs for future device support

---

This story tracks the implementation of the core infrastructure and UI for OP-XY file management and backup/restore via a native companion app.
